messages:
maria: heads up — onboarding sample app (bulk-embed flow) is spiking 429s after the 3rd page. seen on customer demo and local repro.
jon: logs?
maria: paste: ```
[2027-11-02T15:02:10Z] INFO upload page=1 session=abc123 requests=12
[2027-11-02T15:02:11Z] INFO upload page=2 session=abc123 requests=14
[2027-11-02T15:02:12Z] ERROR upload page=3 session=abc123 status=429 body="rate limit exceeded"
[2027-11-02T15:02:12Z] WARN retrying page=3 attempts=1
```
maria: interestingly JS sample doesn't hit this. seems Go SDK client-side batcher is grouping across paginated requests for same session id so concurrency spikes.
kevin: which SDK version? we changed batcher key semantics in 0.12.x to be session-based for sticky batching.
maria: repro using go-sdk v0.12.3 and sample-app v2.2 with default config.
carla: can you share the batcher key calculation?
maria: in vendor go client it's effectively `sessionKey := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", userID, model)` — cursor not included, so multiple pages reuse same key.
carla: that would explain it — if page cursors are processed concurrently they'll merge into one batch and exceed server-side per-session concurrency. JS had cursor in key (hence no issue).
carla: quick patch idea: include pagination cursor (or page index) into the batch key when pagination option is set. patch snippet: ```go
keyParts := []string{opts.UserID, opts.Model}
if opts.Pagination.Cursor != "" {
  keyParts = append(keyParts, "cursor:"+opts.Pagination.Cursor)
}
batchKey := strings.Join(keyParts, "|")
```
jon: nice. does that change any existing behavior for customers who rely on stickiness?
carla: only when pagination is used. we keep old behaviour when Pagination is nil. default is backward compatible.
qa-elaine: can we add unit + integration test that simulates two concurrent page streams with same session id and asserts per-page batching?
carla: yes will add tests. also need e2e with sample-app flags.
sdk-bot: CI triggered for branch fix/pagination-batcher-key (#421) — build queued.
maria: repro steps for QA: 1) checkout sample-app branch reproduce/bulk-pages 2) set env ONBOARD_BURST=1 PAGE_SIZE=100 3) run `go run ./cmd/sample-app --use-go-sdk` 4) watch for repeated 429s on page >=3 with old client, should not occur with patched client.
kevin: for immediate mitigation, can we change client default concurrency to 4 for go-sdk until fix lands? that might avoid spikes for demos.
carla: we could, but I'd rather ship small patch — key change is tiny and low-risk.
maria: also saw token refresh race causing extra retries on 429 — auth/retry stack interacts badly when batcher groups requests. snippet from logs: ```
[...auth] refreshing token concurrently x3
[client] immediate retry -> additional inflight -> 429
```
jon: maybe add a retry jitter and ensure token refresh is singleflight per client.
carla: singleflight is already used, but the batcher change will reduce concurrent inflight. I'll still add a small jitter to retry backoff.
qa-elaine: if we change defaults, let's flag in changelog and on onboarding docs. new onboarding guide should call out "pagination-aware batching" behavior.
maria: agree — customers onboarding with large paginated imports should use the patched go-sdk or tweak concurrency.
carla: i'll open PR with tests + changelog entry. planning to canary deploy to dev cluster tomorrow 10:30 PT.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: dev-cluster, image=sdk-go:fix-pagination-batcher-key, start=2027-11-03T10:30:00-07:00
kevin: :thumbsup: thanks all. will notify support to pause demo escalations until patch is live.
maria: thanks — will post followup after canary results.
